newsitem.title: USA: Key Democrat moves to block antitrust nominee.
newsitem.headline: Key Democrat moves to block antitrust nominee.

text.p: A key Democrat said he plans to block President Clinton's nomination of Joel Klein as chief antitrust enforcer at the Justice Department, the Washington Post reported Tuesday.

Sen. Ernest Hollings, a South Carolina Democrat, told the paper he was concerned that Klein would not do enough to ensure competition in the telecommunications industry after allowing the $21 billion merger of Bell Atlantic Corp. and Nynex Corp. in April.
Klein has been serving as acting assistant attorney general for antitrust since the departure last year of Anne Bingaman.

Hollings' parliamentary "hold" essentially prevents the Senate from voting on the nomination. It follows a hold placed on Klein's nomination by Sen. Conrad Burns, a Montana Republican, who cited concerns that Klein may regulate Bell Atlantic and Nynex, the East Coast's two huge Bell companies, too strongly.
